1943 (second creation)
1966 (third creation) | members_label = Representative | members = Maximo Dalog Jr. | blank1_name = Political party | blank1_info = {{Color box|{{party color|Nacionalista Party}}|border=darkgray}} [[Nacionalista Party|Nacionalista]] | blank2_name = Congressional bloc | blank2_info = Majority }} '''Mountain Province's at-large congressional district''' is the sole [[congressional district of the Philippines]] in the [[Mountain Province]]. It was first created in 1916, when the province was first granted legislative representation in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] under the [[Jones Law (Philippines)|Philippine Autonomy Act]], also known as the Jones Law.{{Cite web |title=Philippine Autonomy Act of 1916 |url=https://lawphil.net/consti/cons1916.html |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=The LawPhil Project |publisher=Arellano Law Foundation, Inc.}} The district was initially composed of the sub-provinces of [[Amburayan]], [[Apayao]], [[Benguet]], [[Bontoc, Mountain Province|Bontoc]], [[Ifugao]], [[Kalinga (province)|Kalinga]], and Lepanto, together with the independent city of [[Baguio]] and the municipalities and municipal districts that had been transferred to the provinces of [[Cagayan]], [[Ilocos Sur]], and [[La Union]], with three members appointed by the [[Governor-General of the Philippines|governor-general]] serving as representatives of the province, although they did not need to be residents of the areas they represented. The Spanish politico-military district of Bontoc, which would later become a sub-province during the American period, was earlier represented in the [[Malolos Congress]] of the [[First Philippine Republic|First Republic]] by a delegate appointed by the president.{{Cite book |last= |url=https://archive.org/details/TheMalolosCongress/page/77/mode/1up |title=The Malolos Congress |date= |publisher=[[National Historical Commission of the Philippines|National Historical Institute]] |year=1999 |isbn=971-538-122-7 |location=Manila, Philippines |pages=77 |language=en-US}} In 1935, the district was divided into three separate [[Single-member district|single-member districts]] for the [[National Assembly of the Philippines#Commonwealth National Assembly|Commonwealth National Assembly]], serving from 1935 to 1941. The three districts would later be dissolved into one two-member at-large districts for the [[National Assembly (Second Philippine Republic)|National Assembly of the Second Republic]]. The district was later re-created in 1966 following the division of the greater Mountain Province into the provinces of Benguet, Ifugao, [[Kalinga-Apayao]], and a smaller Mountain Province,{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=4695|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/7121 |title=An Act Creating the Provinces of Benguet, Mountain Province, Ifugao and Kalinga-Apayao|date=June 18, 1966|accessdate=July 14, 2026}} and reverted to a single-member district for the last legislature of the House of Representatives prior to the imposition of [[Martial law under Ferdinand Marcos|martial law]] from 1969 to 1972. The district served as an electoral district in the [[Philippine Constitutional Convention of 1934|1934 Constitutional Convention]], with two delegates representing each sub-province,{{Cite PH act|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/28/15525|chamber=Act|number=4125|date=May 26, 1934|title=An Act to Provide for the Election and Holding of the Constitutional Convention Authorized by the Act of the Congress of the United States of March Twenty-Fourth, Nineteen Hundred and Thirty-Four, Appropriate Funds Therefor, and for Other Purposes}} and in the [[Philippine Constitutional Convention of 1971|1971 Constitutional Convention]], with two delegates representing Mountain Province at-large.{{Cite PH act|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/14108|chamber=RA|number=6132|date=August 24, 1970|title=An Act Implementing Resolution of Both Houses Numbered Two as Amended by Resolution of Both Houses Numbered Four of the Congress of the Philippines Calling for a Constitutional Convention, Providing for Proportional Representation Therein and Other Details Relating to the Election of Delegates to and the Holding of the Constitutional Convention, Repealing for the Purpose Republic Act Four Thousand Nine Hundred Fourteen, and for Other Purposes}} Following the ratification of the [[Constitution of the Philippines#The 1973 Constitution|1973 Constitution]] and the shift to a [[parliamentary system]], districts were replaced by multi-member regional constituencies, with Mountain Province incorporated into [[Ilocos Region's at-large parliamentary district|Region I's at-large district]] for the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]]. When provincial and city district representation was restored in 1984 for the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]], Mountain Province was represented by one assemblyman.{{Cite PH act|url=https://lawphil.net/executive/proc/proc1984/proc_2332_1984.html|chamber=PP|number=2332|date=February 1, 1984|title=Proclaiming the Ratification in the Plebiscite of January 27, 1984, of the Amendments to the Constitution Embodied in Batasang Pambansa Resolutions Nos. 104, 105, 110, 111, 112 and 113.|access-date=July 14, 2026}} The district was later re-created for the re-established House of Representatives in 1987. It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by Maximo Dalog Jr. of the [[Nacionalista Party]].{{Cite web |title=House Members - 20th Congress |url=https://www.congress.gov.ph/house-members |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]]}} == Recent election results from province-wide races == {| class="wikitable" !
